app.title: Readlang Stats
kpi.total_hint: All words in your Readlang export.
kpi.mature_hint: Words with a review interval of {days}+ days — solid long-term memory.
kpi.young_hint: Words with interval between {young} and {mature} days — actively consolidating.
kpi.learning_hint: Words with interval under 1 day — still in the first-day learning steps.
kpi.new_hint: Words without any successful recall yet.
kpi.avg_easiness_hint: Mean easiness factor across all reviewed words (1.3 = hard, 2.7+ = easy).
kpi.attempts_hint: Sum of all recall attempts across your vocabulary.
kpi.cefr_avg_hint: Average numeric CEFR level among matched words (A1=1 … C2=6).
kpi.streak_current_hint: Consecutive days (ending today) with at least one new word added.
kpi.streak_longest_hint: Your best run of consecutive active days.
kpi.overdue_hint: Words whose scheduled review date has already passed.
kpi.avg_load_hint: Average words due per day over the next 30 days. Peak = the busiest single day.
kpi.avg_cost_hint: Average number of recall attempts among words that reached consolidated status.
chart.status.title: Status distribution
chart.status.hint: Mature — intervals over 3 weeks. Higher mature share means more stable vocabulary.
chart.easiness.title: Easiness factor distribution
chart.easiness.hint: 2.5+ means words are easy. Below 1.8 — problematic zone, worth revisiting context.
chart.velocity.title: Cumulative words added
chart.velocity.hint: Cumulative word count over time. Steep jumps — intensive periods of adding.
chart.heatmap.title: Activity heatmap (last 365 days)
chart.heatmap.hint: Each cell — one day. Darker means more words added. Gaps = days without activity.
chart.weekly.title: Words added per week
chart.weekly.hint: Weekly pace. If bars shrink, you are slowing down.
chart.cefr_profile.title: CEFR level profile
chart.cefr_profile.hint: How many words per CEFR level. More on B1–C1 — deeper vocabulary.
chart.cefr_ease.title: Easiness by CEFR level
chart.cefr_ease.hint: Average easiness per level. If B2/C1 have low easiness — those are your pain zones.
chart.overdue.title: Overdue words
chart.overdue.hint: Words whose scheduled review date has passed. Big list means you fell behind.
chart.calendar.title: Upcoming repetitions (next 60 days)
chart.calendar.hint: Each bar — number of words due that day. Tall bars mean heavy review days ahead.
chart.due_soon.title: Due today and tomorrow
chart.scatter.title: Attempts vs easiness
chart.scatter.hint: Right — more attempts. Down — lower easiness. Colors show CEFR level.
chart.difficult.title: Top difficult words
chart.difficult.hint: Sorted by score = attempts / easiness. Top rows need attention.
chart.recall_ease.title: Self-rated recall ease
chart.recall_ease.hint: 0 = forgot, 5 = remembered easily. Readlang often records 5 by default, so skew to 5 is expected; lower values appear only when you rated 'forgot'.
chart.intervals.title: Interval distribution
chart.intervals.hint: How long until next review. Bigger intervals mean better-consolidated words.
chart.time_of_day.title: Additions by hour (UTC)
chart.time_of_day.hint: When you tend to add new words. UTC, so adjust for your timezone.
chart.next_year.title: Review load — next 365 days
chart.next_year.hint: Scheduled reviews per day. Peaks mean heavy days ahead — plan accordingly.
table.score_hint: attempts / easiness. Higher — harder to learn.
editor.title: Edit words
editor.not_in_context: ⚠ Word not found in context. Backend will reject this change.
settings.title: Settings
bulk.title: Paste JSON from the LLM
bulk.step2_hint: Send the exported JSON to an LLM, ask it to improve contexts / translations / words, then paste its reply here. The reply must be the same array — the `word` field is the anchor and must not change. To rename a word, add a `new_word` field. Line breaks inside strings must be escaped as \n.
bulk.step3_hint: Red text was removed, green was added, gray is unchanged. Uncheck rows you don't want. Conflicts are not auto-selected — fix them or uncheck them.
bulk.conflicts: Conflicts: {n} — fix these or uncheck them before applying
